Later transfer to Amman overnight.

Arrive Cairo, the Egyptian capital city and transfer to a hotel.

Itinerary: 


Day1: ARRIVAL – Marrakech

Transfer arrival from Menara Marrakech airport to your hotel in marrakech . Overnight at the hotel in Marrakech.
Possibility of a city Tour depending on arrival time.

 

Day2: Marrakech - Ouzoud - Marrakech   

After breakfast, departure to Ouzoud Falls is one of the top natural sights in Morocco. You’ll head into the middle Atlas Mountains to see North Africa’s highest waterfall . You should bring a good pair of walking shoes. Cross the river on a hand-powered barge, visit cafes at the edge of the water, or check out the Barbary apes that live in the lush river valley.
Enjoy a Moroccan lunch at your leisure in one of the local cafes or restaurants of the Ouzoud Falls (not included). We drive back to Marrakech. Have a time to be ready for starting the Moroccan Taste of riad Special Diner in the warm atmosphere of a beautiful Riad in Medina, experience the real taste of Morocco with traditional food, excellent service end classic entertainment, with a folkloric show and belly dancer. Overnight at the hotel in Marrakech.

 

Day 3 : Marrakech - Ait Ben Haddou- Ouarzazate - Merzouga   

After breakfast early morning departure, to Marzouga via the high Atlas Mountains, the Great Atlas through the Tichca Pass   at the height of 2260, Kasbah of Ait Ben Haddou and the old Telltouba. These two fortified villages, recognized in the  UNESCO World Heritage, provide a complete view of the techniques of building old mud houses. Arrival in Ouarzazate, Originally a crossing point for traders crossing the Sahara Desert, this UNESCO world heritage site is equally recognized as the location for films such as ‘Laurence of Arabia’ and ‘Gladiators. reaching the Erg Chebbi, refreshing with mint tea, & picked up by 4x4 vehicles to the camp, Sunset Or Sunrise Camel excursion. Enjoy dinner, camp fire with local music under the bright stars, free time and overnight stay in your private Royal tent.

 

Day4 : Merzouga - Thinghir - Marrakech 

After breakfast, the journey starts with the visit Todra gorges and valley then drive to Tinghir, passing by the beautiful city in Morocco famous for roses` plantation “Kallat M’Gouna. Then Continue to marrakech. Overnight at the hotel in Marrakech.

 

Day 5 : Marrakech - Essaouira       

Breakfast at the hotel and head to beautiful Essaouira on the Atlantic Coast. Once you arrive at the port city, formerly known as Mogador, you will meet the local guide and you will have time to enjoy the charming sights of Essaouira.

Take pictures of its ocher-colored walls, the beautiful and vibrant Moulay El Hassan square, the markets also known as souks, as well as the little streets of the city`s old Medina, see the local markets, and wow at the gems in the jeweler`s quarter. Then, lunch in a local restaurant. During your trip, you`ll also visit an association of Berber women producing argan oil.

Overnight at the hotel in Essaouira.

 

Day6: Essaouira – Agadir

This spectacular road winds for about 176 km between the sea and the desert. The surface of the road is fine. It is slow and winding but it doesn`t have any steep drop-offs or narrow bits. The surface is in good condition and would be fine even in the rain. There are plenty of places that will make you want to stop,. Arriving hotel Situated mere steps from the golden swathe of Taghazout Beach. Overnight at the hotel in Taghazout.

 

Day7 : Agadir

Start the day with breakfast at the hotel followed by Discover the city . The city tour will include the most stunning sites in Agadir. The city center: The Kasbah ; The Ports; Ancienne Talborjt : old Agadir town and constitutes a mass grave for all those who died in the 1960 earthquake. Cooperative of argan: informative visit to the women’s cooperative that produce culinary and cosmetic oils. Presentation of the argane and its products. The souk el Had in Arabic means Sunday market , stretched on thirteen hectares (it is the largest market in Morocco), with walls up to six meters and with thirteen gates.There are 2000 retailers selling food, and souvenir buying, the atmosphere here alone makes the trip worthwhile. It’s a total sensory immersion, and a wonderful place in which to get lost for a while. Overnight at the hotel in Taghazout.

 

Day8 : Departure

Check out after breakfast at the hotel. Then road to Marrakech Menara Airport according to the flight time.

Cross the Strait of Gibraltar to visit the north of Morocco on a day trip from Malaga. A former international city during the Spanish and French protectorate, today it is the most important city in the north of the Kingdom of Morocco.
 
Total duration of the excursion about 13 hours.
 
Departure from Malaga to the port of Tarifa, where we will embark on a fast boat; after approximately 45 minutes of crossing, we will arrive at the port of Tangier, where our local guide will be waiting for us. During the boat trip we will cross the Strait of Gibraltar, admiring all the views of the Spanish and African coasts.
We will start with a panoramic bus tour, leaving the port and crossing the modern city with its hotels, boulevards and former embassies, now consulates. Arriving at the outskirts of the city, we will pass near the palace of the King of Morocco, the governor of Tangier, until we reach one of the viewpoints over the Strait of Gibraltar, from where we will contemplate the best view of the Spanish coast, and the union of the Atlantic Ocean with the Mediterranean Sea. Arriving at the old city, we will visit the Kasbah, the Medina, the market and a typical Moroccan bazaar, where you can admire the typical crafts of the country and make purchases. After visiting the old city on foot, with its narrow streets and squares, we will go to a restaurant where we will have a typical Moroccan lunch. After lunch we will return to the port to return to Spain. For this excursion it is essential to have a passport and national identity card for citizens of the European Union.
 
The excursion includes:
- Transport by coach round trip

I hope this email finds you well and excited about the upcoming trip to Morocco! We`re thrilled to have you join us for what promises to be an unforgettable experience. To ensure you have all the necessary information and resources to make the most of your journey, we`ve put together this guidebook and essential information package tailored specifically for the guests.

1. Confirmation Voucher and Travel Document

Attached to this email, you`ll find our comprehensive guidebook to Morocco. It includes detailed insights into Moroccan culture, etiquette tips, essential Arabic phrases, and must-visit destinations across the country. Whether you`re wandering through the bustling streets of Marrakech, exploring the ancient ruins of Fez, or marveling at the breathtaking landscapes of the Sahara Desert, this guidebook will serve as your trusted companion throughout your adventure.

3. Travel Essentials:

  • Passport and Visa: Please ensure that your passport is valid for at least six months beyond your planned departure date. American citizens do not need a visa for tourist visits to Morocco lasting less than 90 days.

  • Currency: The currency used in Morocco is the Moroccan Dirham (MAD). While credit cards are widely accepted in major cities, it`s advisable to carry some cash for smaller purchases and transactions.

  • Weather and Clothing: Morocco experiences diverse climates, ranging from the Mediterranean along the coast to desert inland. Pack accordingly, including lightweight clothing for warmer days and layers for cooler evenings. Modest clothing is recommended, especially when visiting religious sites.

  • Health and Safety:  It`s essential to stay hydrated and protect yourself from the sun, especially in desert regions. We recommend carrying bottled water with you at all times.

4. Cultural Etiquette:

  • Greetings: A handshake is the most common form of greeting in Morocco. When addressing someone, it`s polite to use titles such as "Mr." (Sidi), "Mrs." (Sitt), or "Miss" (Sbrou).

  • Dress Code: While Morocco is relatively liberal, particularly in tourist areas, it`s respectful to dress modestly, especially when visiting religious sites or rural communities.

  • Photography: Always ask for permission before taking photos of people, particularly in more remote or traditional areas.

If you have any questions or require further assistance before your trip, please don`t hesitate to reach out to us. We`re here to ensure that your journey to Morocco is as seamless and enjoyable as possible.
